Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB415.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Miaoyun of Dabei. Miaoyun Zhenxiong owns the retained prayer: hill-earth scorched to flowing metal, sea-water boiling — the four seas and five lakes, stones out and waters fallen — then the old dragon palace shaken, rain pouring like an overturned bowl: spirit power, or the way of things?

Senses.Explanation: The four seas and five lakes of the Chan records: the everywhere-at-once — the realm under the sovereign's sway in the old couplet, the four-seas folk sealed in one retreat, the dragon-world of the retirement verse, and the drought-bared lake stones. Wuzu Fayan closes his self-portrait with the line Yangshan once spoke — two mouths, one no-tongue, a man of the four seas and five lakes: in the full sunlight, does he glimpse or not?, Cishou Huaishen opens the summer retreat: people of the four seas and five lakes, Huilin seals the feet with you — like learning to herd the ox, body and mind to be seasoned; plow your own field, infringe no other's grain; one line off, and what face for the ninety days?, Chijue Daochong at his retirement: wanting to go, going hinders; wanting to stay, staying hinders — originally no hindrance: the crane-heaven of the ten isles and three islands, the dragon-world of the four seas and five lakes, and Tiantong Rujing seals his hall address — after all, how? The four seas and five lakes under the imperial sway, the peace that has no image yet has its origin. Juyun Chuiwan Guangzhen takes the Zhaozhou cloth-shirt ask — same or different from the first principle? — same: the Lang and Li rivers' water, the four seas and five lakes under the sovereign's sway; different: the bean-mountain drums of cracked tiles, the white rain below Yanghu; neither same nor different: the Tengwang pavilion over the river, the jade pendants and ringing bells done with their dance, Eryin Mi at the new year: the myriad forms fresh-aired, the four seas and five lakes wave on wave clear, the capital gardens' willows green — and the staff that spring cannot change nor autumn wither, and Miaoyun Zhenxiong prays the drought down: hill-earth scorched to flowing metal, sea-water boiling, crops withered, bamboo and trees shrunk — the four seas and five lakes, stones out and waters fallen — then the old dragon palace shaken, thunder and lightning, rain pouring bowl-over: spirit power, or the way of things?
